title: Oscar and the Postcard
premise: Mara Halloran's vineyard is drowning in debt left by her late father, and the only lifeline is a buyout offer from her cousin's development syndicate. When she hires Oscar Reyes, a charming stranger from the postcard shop, to pose as her boyfriend at the family reunion, their fake romance turns real — and Oscar reveals he's an investigator who believes her father's debts were forged by that same cousin. Together they uncover the paper trail, confront the family at a final harvest dinner, and Mara chooses justice over the vineyard itself; in the end, she keeps only the small parcel where her father first planted vines, replants it with Oscar, and says the sentence they've both rehearsed: 'I'm staying.'
about_author: Wendell Whitlock is the pen name of a former estate lawyer who traded depositions for love stories set in wine country. He writes about families that break promises and strangers who keep them.

chapters.title: The Stranger on the Postcard Rack
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Drowning in foreclosure notices, Mara meets Oscar in a dusty postcard shop where he buys a card of her own vineyard every week. Impulsive and desperate, she asks him to be her fake boyfriend for Saturday's reunion. The beat: wary hope disguised as a business transaction.

chapters.title: Reunion, With Witnesses
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the reunion, Oscar plays the role too well — and quietly photographs documents while cousin Randall toasts 'family legacy.' By dessert, the fake kiss feels real, and Oscar spots a signature on Mara's father's loan papers that isn't his. The beat: desire tangled with deception, guilt blooming.

chapters.title: What the Ink Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Oscar confesses he's been investigating Randall's forgery scheme for years — his own family lost their farm to it. Mara, furious at being used, helps him trace the forged signatures anyway, and they find the original ledger hidden in her father's cellar. The beat: betrayal giving way to partnership, grief becoming purpose.

chapters.title: The Sentence We Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the harvest dinner, they present the evidence; Randall is exposed before the whole family and the syndicate collapses. Mara signs away most of the vineyard to settle the debts, keeping one hillside. She tells Oscar the rehearsed sentence — 'I'm staying' — and he answers with the postcard he never mailed: her vineyard, addressed to her. The beat: release, justice, and chosen love.
